bug_semantics: CWE-367 TOCTOU in OcspServerCertificateValidator.userEventTriggered: on SslHandshakeCompletionEvent the handler immediately ctx.fireUserEventTriggered(evt) and only then starts async OcspClient.query. Downstream client handlers treat TLS as complete and can write application data (or consume server bytes) to a revoked peer during the OCSP window; a later REVOKED result closes the channel too late. Original code also removed itself from the pipeline before the OCSP future completed, so it could not hold inbound data.
flaw_origin: The fire-then-query order was the original design of the new netty-handler-ssl-ocsp module, not a later regression. PR #12898 (GitHub squash 09ac33766f6c30d445dcdfb4285f589aedf5d7fe onto 4.1) reconstructed to single member 6d1b5b0908d3833c81973a54ae411a8d4809fc64, which first added OcspServerCertificateValidator.java with ctx.fireUserEventTriggered(evt) at the top of userEventTriggered before OcspClient.query. That blob is identical on the squash landing. Later 4.1/4.2 edits (assert fix 8b34a81a08, lambda rewrite 0e1d7dfd46) kept the immediate fire. GHSA #17063 delayed the handshake event until OCSP finished and buffered reads.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-56822 / GHSA-wc96-39fc-566f is a published, non-withdrawn TOCTOU in OcspServerCertificateValidator. The attack is the handshake-complete event reaching downstream handlers before async OCSP can revoke/close, leaking application data to a revoked server. The sink is the immediate ctx.fireUserEventTriggered(evt) at the start of userEventTriggered plus removing the handler before the OCSP future completes. First-write search used git log -S on that fire call and the new-file introduction of OcspServerCertificateValidator.java. Public 4.1 history first contains the file in GitHub squash 09ac33766f6c30d445dcdfb4285f589aedf5d7fe (PR #12898). That squash is not the BIC: GitHub still serves the single PR member 6d1b5b0908d3833c81973a54ae411a8d4809fc64 with the identical validator blob, and that member's parent fe0b5ce16c4508387f999e530a85f2d968e90a3c lacks the path. 6d1b5b09 is therefore the smallest reconstructed first-write; 09ac337 is the 4.1 carrier (ancestor of 4.1.86.Final and 4.2.0.Final; absent from 4.1.85.Final). Later refactors did not introduce the race. Fix: 4.2 squash 5b68c61f37aa4a3045cba624cbea239655c9003b lands the delay-and-buffer change in 4.2.16.Final; reconstructed direct patch is 1c7bf683ac381665736d5bfea49e8e81a27ddac7 (parent still fire-first). 4.1 equivalent landing bb2ff68a1fb71cb4b0eb9a9e17b66c52aff680c6 is in 4.1.136.Final. AI judgment is BIC-object only: 6d1b5b09 is human Aayush Atharva with no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/Made-with/bot marker; the squash landing is the same human author with GitHub as committer and no AI trailer. PR-body and later AI-only-on-fix signals were not used. Verdict NOT_AI.
